text: It refines the regulatory framework, strengthens system implementation, and drives businesses to continuously improve energy efficiency.

speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Energy efficiency remains one of the most practical and cost-effective ways for Singapore to enhance energy security, reduce emissions and strengthen long-term economic competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: That was a very strong and passionate speech in Chinese.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With the ongoing Middle East conflict driving volatility in global energy supply and prices, energy efficiency is not just about sustainability.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is a critical pillar of Singapore's energy resilience.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If we are serious about our net-zero ambitions and resilience, then energy efficiency must remain a foundational pillar of our strategy.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Bill strengthens the Energy Conservation Act by closing an important gap.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Today, MEPS and labelling requirements apply mainly to goods supplied locally.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I support the intent of the Bill but would like to raise several implementation considerations.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: A key question is how enforcement will work in practice, particularly for small-scale imports.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Increasingly, individuals and small businesses procure equipment through e-commerce platforms and parcel shipments.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While each import may be small, the cumulative impact could be significant.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Given the scale and speed of online commerce, could the Minister clarify whether NEA has sufficient enforcement capacity, and how it intends to prioritise and operationalise these expanded responsibilities?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State clarify how enforcement will be carried out for imports intended for a person's own use, particularly through online marketplaces or small parcel deliveries?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Will there be thresholds below which enforcement becomes impractical and, if so, how do we ensure that this does not create loopholes?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Related to this, there may be scope to integrate enforcement across agencies.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, in sectors, such as F&B, where businesses import equipment directly, could existing inspection regimes, such as Singapore Food Agency's inspections for licensing, also incorporate checks on energy efficiency compliance and registration?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This would reduce duplication of enforcement resources and strengthen on-the-ground compliance.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Second, on regulatory burden and impact on businesses.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Could this create unnecessary duplication and administrative burden, particularly for SMEs importing small quantities?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Would the Ministry consider a shared product registry that allows for product-level registration, while still maintaining accountability at the importer level?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: More broadly, many SMEs import specialised equipment for their own operations.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Will there be a simplified compliance pathway for low-volume importers or SMEs, so that compliance costs remain proportionate and do not become a barrier to business operations?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Third, on consumer awareness and the digital marketplace.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As more consumers purchase appliances online, they may unknowingly buy non-compliant products.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The Bill allows for waivers where compliance with requirements may not be possible in specific cases.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Could the Minister clarify the criteria and safeguards for granting such waivers, and how consistency will be ensured?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It would be important to avoid unintended circumvention or uneven application across businesses.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I note that there will be a transition period before full implementation.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State share how the Government intends to mitigate any potential surge in imports of non-compliant equipment ahead of the enforcement date?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Without appropriate safeguards, there may be a risk of front-loading less efficient equipment into the system.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It closes an emerging gap, reinforces fairness and supports our broader energy transition.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With the right attention to implementation, enforcement and business impact, I believe it will achieve its intended outcomes.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: As a resource-constrained nation that imports almost all of its energy, we must continue to treat efficiency not as an option, but as a necessity, both to manage costs and to meet our climate commitments.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Earlier, Members also touched on MEPS and MELS.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: In this regard, both MEPS and MELS are effective policy tools.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: MEPS play a critical role in removing less efficient products from the market.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: It sets the minimum level of energy efficiency that appliances must meet before they can even be sold in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: In other words, if it wastes too much energy, it does not make the cut.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: As for MELS, as earlier mentioned by another Member, Best Denki was his choice, it is that that familiar "tick label" we see on our appliances.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The more ticks, the more energy-efficient the product and the more we save on electricity bill.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: It helps us make smarter and more energy-efficient purchasing decisions.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Together, both MEPS and MELS have shaped market behaviour and raised overall energy performance standards.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: The proposed extension of these frameworks to end-user imports is a logical and a necessary step.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: By ensuring that even goods imported for own use meet baseline efficiency standards, we strengthen the integrity of our regulatory regime and promote more responsible energy consumption across the board.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: First, on the compliance framework and its practical implications.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: However, they will inevitably introduce additional compliance steps for businesses and individuals.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: It is therefore important that implementation remains practical and proportionate.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Additionally, I urge the Government to consider creating a priority processing lane perhaps for SMEs that register products with energy ratings exceeding the current MEPS.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: By fast-tracking high-efficiency products, the Government would provide SMEs with a competitive edge over larger competitors.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Without such accommodations, we risk placing a disproportionate burden on smaller players.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: I would also appreciate clarification on how the Government intends to ensure compliance in respect of online marketplaces, where many such transactions increasingly take place.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: This brings me to my second point: the role of online platforms and enforcement.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: In addition, stronger communication mechanisms between regulators and platform providers will be necessary to ensure that non-compliant listings are swiftly identified and removed.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Without such upstream measures, enforcement risks becoming reactive rather than preventive.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: For these measures to gain broad-based support, we must recognise that higher-efficiency products often come with higher upfront costs.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: While such products typically deliver long-term savings through reduced energy consumption, the initial price difference will still pose a barrier, particularly for households and SMEs.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: In addition, bulk procurement programmes and partnerships with retailers could help lower prices and encourage wider adoption, especially among SMEs.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: At the same time, public education remains key.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Continued efforts to raise awareness of the long-term cost savings and environmental benefits of energy efficiency will help shift mindsets and strengthen public support.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: However, to ensure that these measures receive broad support, the Government must acknowledge that energy-saving products that are highly efficient typically come with higher upfront costs.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: While such products will result in long-term savings through lower energy consumption, the initial price difference can still be a barrier and obstacle, especially for the low-income as well as small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, to address this matter, the Government should consider support measures, such as rebates, grants or co-financing schemes, to help reduce upfront costs, which are essentially efforts to ensure energy-efficient equipment is more accessible to Singaporeans and businesses.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Additionally, collaboration with businesses can also help lower prices and encourage wider adoption, particularly among SMEs.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: At the same time, public education is also very important.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Continuous efforts to increase awareness and understanding about long-term cost savings and environmental benefits as well as prioritising energy efficiency will help change mindsets and strengthen community support.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Therefore, it is important for the Government to expand its awareness campaigns by partnering with schools, social media as well as community organisations in various languages, to educate consumers from the young ones to senior citizens.

speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
text: Training for businesses can also play a role in providing clear explanations and instil confidence in consumers, and this should be conducted more frequently and thoroughly.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, would you like to adjourn the debate?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With the escalating war in the Middle East threatening the Strait of Hormuz, a lifeline for nearly one-fifth of global oil, volatile markets and rising prices are not distant news.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We cannot control global supply, but we can control our dependence on it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As Chair of the Defence and Foreign Affairs Government Parliamentary Committee, I see energy security as inseparable from national security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Every watt we save is a watt we do not have to import for.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I support this Bill because it closes a critical gap.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A gap in policy becomes a liability in a crisis.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It allows inefficient equipment to be locked into our system and lets those who bypass the rules undercut compliant businesses.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Even if direct imports are less than 10% today, we must close this gap before it grows.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What we allow into our system today determines the bills we pay tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The principles of this Bill are sound, but its success depends on implementation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: To ensure it works fairly and affordably on the ground, I have four areas of clarification.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We know that energy efficient products are cheaper over time.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, most energy efficient products come with a premium.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Households and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) do not live in lifecycle calculations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They live with immediate budgets and cash flow constraints.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are we doing enough to help households and businesses bridge the gap between higher upfront costs and lower long-term savings?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are existing schemes such as the Climate Friendly Household Programme, the Energy Efficiency Grant and the Resource Efficiency Grant sufficient for those most affected?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will compliant models remain competitively priced, or will a persistent green premium emerge?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will the Ministry ensure that grants and subsidies remain responsive to market price fluctuations, so that no household or SME is left behind?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The right choice must also be the affordable choice.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir, consumer protection in the digital marketplace.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Bill empowers the Government to regulate online advertisements, require energy efficiency information and take down non-compliant listings.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will platforms be required to screen listings before they appear, rather than only remove them after a breach is reported?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will consumers have a simple and accessible way to verify whether a product is compliant before making a purchase?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If a non-compliant listing is removed after payment has been made, what protections will consumers have?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will marketplace operators be required to facilitate refunds or stop deliveries?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will responsibility be allocated among marketplace operators, sellers and importers?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Consumer protection must begin before check-out, not after complaints.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With the new requirements, importers must register goods, maintain records and potentially provide samples for testing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How onerous will these compliance requirements be, particularly for individuals and SMEs importing for their own use?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If compliance is too complex, compliance will fail.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Bill grants the Director-General the power to impose, modify, or revoke conditions even after registration.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What principles will guide the exercise of these powers and will they be clearly communicated to businesses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Why do such decisions take effect immediately even when an appeal is filed?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As new offences are introduced, including cases where goods are later used in ways that would have made the original import non-compliant, how will the Government distinguish between deliberate circumvention and genuine misunderstanding?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry provide regular reporting to Parliament on waivers granted, appeals outcomes and enforcement trends?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because energy conservation does not begin and end with regulation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The International Energy Agency has outlined practical measures to reduce demand quickly, including working from home, reducing unnecessary travel, improving driving efficiency and encouraging public transport use.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The cheapest energy is the energy we do not use.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the public sector lead the way by institutionalising air-conditioning temperature standards across Government buildings?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are we promoting operational efficiency across our fleets and industries, such as incentivising eco-driving certifications for commercial fleets?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Does the Ministry have a playbook for temporary, targeted conservation measures, such as remote work arrangements or speed limit adjustments, should supply disruptions worsen?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because energy security is built not just by policy, but by behaviour, incentives and collective discipline.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We began this speech with a world in crisis, where conflict far beyond our shores can disrupt something as fundamental as energy.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Whether consumers will be protected in the digital marketplace.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And whether enforcement powers will be exercised transparently.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have also suggested that beyond regulation, we must act decisively to reduce demand and strengthen efficiency.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many of us are familiar with MEPS as well as MELS.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will ensure consistent application of the requirements, while also not overly restricting consumer choices.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I would like to highlight two clauses in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify why this is required?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Is the intent to keep track of the identity and number of importers of the specific regulated goods, even if it has already been registered by an importer?

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Regardless, would the agency consider a more streamlined approach for subsequent importers of already registered regulated goods.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, can the agency update the specific model/type of regulated good(s) in its Database of Registered Goods for general awareness that it has been registered, and waive certain requirements for subsequent importers, such as the requirement to provide test reports, ISO certifications and so on, which would already have been provided by the original importer.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would reduce the regulatory burden for subsequent importers.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is quite likely that for importers who are importing for their own use to only import one piece of the good, so it could perhaps, be challenging for them to provide “free of charge” samples to the Director-General for the purpose of testing and analysis.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I seek a clarification again on the need for this.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would also like to highlight two points in relation to the implementation of the amendments in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, the extension of the MEPS and MELS requirements to importers will likely rely on existing processes for the registration of the regulated goods.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, the existing processes, as I understand, are designed for suppliers, retailers, importers and manufacturers that supply or sell regulated goods.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is important therefore that the registration processes be modified or streamlined to be relevant for individual importers, including individuals or households that do the same.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For example, the current Energy Labelling Scheme (ELS) Portal for registration relies on Corppass, which are for businesses and companies.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It may also need to be adapted to allow for the use of Singpass by individual importers.

speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I urge the agency to consider whether these charges for individual importers can be waived or whether there can be a tiered registration system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All the Members who have spoken had indicated their support for the Bill and its intent to extend MEPS and MELS to regulated goods imported by end users for own use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In answering their questions and comments, I would like to begin by clarifying that only certain common appliances, such as air-conditioners and refrigerators are covered under the Energy Conservation Act and this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, equipment, such as electric vehicles chargers, are not currently covered under the Energy Conservation Act and National Environment Agency's (NEA's) website has a list of regulated goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The volume of regulated goods imported for own use is small for now especially when we consider appliances, such as air-conditioners and refrigerators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The concern is that this could increase over time given the proliferation of online marketplaces, making it easier for consumers to import such regulated goods for their use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Several Members have asked about the Government's plans to reduce compliance burden for end users arising from the proposed amendments and have made suggestions to streamline the registration process and user journey, such as waiving test report requirements for regulated goods if these Goods had been demonstrated to be MEPS-compliant by prior importers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The stakeholders we have consulted, which range from local suppliers of regulated goods, businesses and technical experts from our institutes of higher learning have all been broadly supportive of the proposed amendments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have also provided feedback to reduce the compliance requirements and ensure practicality for end users and we have incorporated their feedback into this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Lights are less energy intensive compared to other regulated goods and typically consumer 10 times less energy than appliances, such as refrigerators, and constitute less than 6% of household energy consumption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to monitor the import of lights for own use and if needed, explore the extension of regulations to cover such imports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Currently, local suppliers are subject to a registration fee of about $70 per model to register their models for local supply with NEA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The reason for this is, there needs to then be an assignment of responsibility for the act of importing this particular good and that this particular report matches the good as declared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And so, it is the person who is conducting the import for own use who has to take on that responsibility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA can accept test reports provided by equipment manufacturers for registration of regulated goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Suppliers and end users are not required to obtain additional independent test reports beyond those provided by the equipment manufacturers for registration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To avoid incurring unnecessary import costs, end users are also encouraged to register their regulated good prior to import to ensure that the good is MEPS- and MELS-compliant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As I have previously explained, to do so prior to import incurs no cost for the end user importing for their own use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to review and streamline the registration process as needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA will upgrade the ELS Portal for a better user experience for those applying to register their appliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: End users will be able to use Singpass, similar to how businesses currently use Corppass to access the ELS Portal and register.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA will provide more information in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Foo Cexiang highlighted challenges for individuals and households in providing free samples of the regulated goods imported for own use, which the Director-General may require under clause 12 of the Bill for the purpose of testing or analysis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Act does provide levers for NEA to obtain samples to, such as in the case of a business that may bulk import regulated goods for their own use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But I would like to assure Mr Foo and Members of the House that testing analysis is only conducted on regulated goods on a needs-basis and only where it is feasible to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Muhaimin Malik asked about the Government's approach to allow the Director-General to exercise powers to impose, modify or revoke conditions after registration and the approach for appeals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There will be instances where the Government would require swift rectifications to prevent the further circulation or further sale of non-compliant regulated goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As set out in clause 7 of the Bill, the Director-General must, before imposing or modifying any condition for registration, give written notice to the holder of the registration stating the proposed condition or modification, and provide time for the holder of the registration to make written representations with regard to the proposed modifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Act also expressly allows any importer or manufacturer aggrieved by the decision to file an appeal to the Minister.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how the Government would ensure regulated goods would remain MEPS-compliant after import, particularly those controlled by the manufacturers or third parties through software embedded within the regulated goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To balance the regulatory burden and energy efficiency outcomes, we have adopted a practical approach to apply MEPS and MELS requirements at the point of import only for own use, similar to the current regulations that apply requirements at the point of local supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And I would emphasise this point that this is the regime that is in place currently for local suppliers, and the opportunities and hypotheticals that Mr Dennis Tan had provided within the speech potentially exist today, but they do not appear to be a material problem at this point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Nevertheless, we will continue to monitor the situation and if NEA has information that approved regulated goods have low energy efficiencies during actual operation, we will investigate, conduct additional tests and audits and follow-up as necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: SMEs may import regulated goods for own use through intermediaries, such as contractors or interior designers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In such cases, it is the intermediary importing the regulated goods for subsequent supply to the SME that would be responsible for compliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Like all other end users directly import regulated goods for their own use, franchisees must ensure that the regulated goods that they import for their own use comply with the MEPS and MELS requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA will issue press releases and circulars to inform end users and businesses about the new regulations and will also engage key stakeholders, including the food and beverage businesses through industry associations, such as the Restaurant Association of Singapore, to ensure that businesses and industries understand the new regulations and their responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA will also conduct checks on business establishments as needed, and conduct enforcement in response to whistle-blowing reports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have assessed that there is no need to introduce controls at the point of import at this time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the questions around Singapore Customs, and the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority, we have assessed that there is no need for these types of controls at this point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The number of regulated goods imported for own use is expected to be small.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And if there were such controls as some Members have asked, they would apply to all regulated goods imported for local supply or own use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This potentially increases the administrative burden, friction and compliance costs for the importers significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And today, the vast majority of regulated goods brought into Singapore meant for local supply are already MEPS- and MELS-compliant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: What we are trying to do is close the loophole for a small number of goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This ensures that the non-compliant regulated goods, such as those that do not carry the MELS labels, are not offered to end users in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The actual operationalisation of removal of these listings will be done by the platform.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is NEA providing an enforcement instruction and it is the platform then will have to comply about how these are taken down.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Consumers can verify compliance by checking for accompanying MELS labels when purchasing regulated goods through online platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The new regulations also exclude second-hand or used regulated goods, whether it is online or in the physical marketspace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Notwithstanding this, second-hand regulated goods imported into Singapore for resale as brand-new will be subject to the MEPS and MELS requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since 2023, NEA has also been engaging online platforms, such as Shopee and Lazada, to remove advertisements of non-compliant goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The online platforms engaged have also cooperated with NEA's instructions and have taken down the non-complaint listings accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Moving forward, we will continue to work closely with online platforms to enhance surveillance of the online space and to encourage the proactive removal of listings of non-compliant regulated goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The platforms may implement manual or algorithmic systems at their discretion to proactively remove these listings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If NEA discovers online listings that are non-compliant, we will work with the platforms to manually remove such listings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope this will minimise the purchase of non-compliant regulated goods, unintended or otherwise, by individuals and households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have assessed the accompanying penalty framework to be a sufficient deterrent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The MEPS-compliant equipment delivers life-cycle energy savings compared to energy inefficient equipment and this actually already intrinsically incentivises end users to import compliant equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, the risk of reputational damage from the legal proceedings also discourages businesses from importing non-compliant goods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Put all of that together, we think this is likely to be quite effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members had asked how the Government would provide support to businesses and households to adopt more energy-efficient equipment and to build energy management capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have a suite of measures that businesses and households can tap on to strengthen their energy resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Companies can tap on the Energy Efficiency Grant to co-fund investments in energy-efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Energy Efficiency Grant already covers a wide range of regulated goods, including air-conditioners, refrigerators, clothes dryers, motors and water heaters today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a part of the measures to support more businesses in purchasing energy efficient equipment through the increasingly uncertain global climate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I encourage businesses to use the Energy Efficiency Grant to adopt more energy efficient equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This helps to offset the initial cost of purchase of more resource-efficient household appliances and fittings, which are expected to yield recurring energy and water savings over their lifespan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Households that have yet to use their $400 Climate Vouchers can do so up to 31 December 2027.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More recently, we expanded the list of products under the enhanced Climate Friendly Households Programme to include induction stoves and five-tick clothes dryers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: From 15 April 2026, households can tap on Climate Vouchers to access a wider range of resource-efficient products and achieve greater resource efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We do also want to invest in the development of a pipeline of energy management professionals to support energy efficiency initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Lee Hong Chuang suggested that the Government strengthen cooperation between industry and higher education institutions to develop more professional courses in energy efficiency and energy management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Member would be pleased to hear that this is already happening and that the Government has programmes in place to help businesses build a pipeline of energy management professionals to support our resource efficiency initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, in February 2026, NEA, the Singapore Institute of Technology and the Energy Efficiency Training Centre launched the new Energy Efficiency Training Facility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This supports the delivery of programmes, such as the Energy Efficiency Upskilling Programme and Singapore Certified Energy Manager Programme, to develop a pipeline of local energy management talent and to build local energy efficiency capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members made several suggestions to strengthen public education and incentivise the adoption of compliant goods and were concerned about the cost impact to end users when the amendments take effect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: NEA maintains an online database of compliant regulated goods with product information, including estimated annual energy consumption and energy costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Energy efficient appliances typically offer lower life-cycle costs through energy savings, even if they may have higher upfront capital costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill is a necessary step to ensure that all regulated goods in Singapore are held to the same MEPS and MELS requirements and deliver greater energy efficiency outcomes for end users.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Clarifications for Senior Minister of State Dr Janil?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: I believe my questions in my speech were not addressed in the Senior Minister of State's reply.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: I asked at the end of my speech, regarding the food and beverage sector alone, with the large numbers of restaurants and food and beverage establishments in the high churn, there must be a lot of freezers, chillers, refrigerators; and what would be the estimated annual consumption, and with this transition to all MEPS-compliant equipment, what will be the reduction like, in terms of the energy savings?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: And secondly, with these large numbers of end users and end equipment, what is the process that is needed to actually enforce this new requirement?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: And I hope that this process and the requirements will not be too onerous.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Otherwise, it will just end up conserving energy on one part and expending more energy in terms of human resources to carry out the enforcement.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The answer to the first part is, we do not yet know because the extension of the Energy Conservation Act is to goods that are currently not regulated.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have engagements with the sector, with the restaurant association, we have information that the behaviour is happening.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But until we regulate these goods, we will not have a handle on exactly how many there are coming into the space.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, is that overall energy reduction in the sector?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think we cannot draw a straight line because it is not the only consumption of energy within the sector.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But the short answer is, the current issue is that we do not regulate the goods that we are going to regulate, and so we do not know exactly how many there are on the market.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The second part of the question that this involves a large number; actually, this is not the case.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is a not a huge number that will have to then come on to the scheme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have engaged with those that we can find and we have worked with them to then shape the operations of the scheme to ensure that it is not too onerous, as I described in my speech.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Just one clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, if a software update is found to significantly degrade the energy performance of hardware already in use, what specific enforcement action will NEA take?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Specifically, would the registration of those regulated goods be retrospectively revoked and would this result in a mandate for the user to cease usage or for the manufacturer to force a software roll-back?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Act provides for the Director-General and NEA to exercise a range of measures should they come across a good, which is non-compliant or which was declared to be compliant and is now subsequently non-compliant.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And that can arise for a number of reasons.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Software modification is one, but physical hardware modification is also another.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Failing which, warnings and fines, all are possible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If we are aware that a particular model or particular manufacturer may engage in such practices, when further models from that manufacturer are submitted for review and registration, certainly, we would have to take this into account.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, we would have a range of possible responses to such behaviour.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I would encourage businesses and end users, please do not engage in such behaviour.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The intent of these regulations is to improve our energy efficiency and by doing so, we will end up lowering the costs for all the businesses and the households that are involved, and that is the important outcome that we want to achieve.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Looks like there are no further clarifications.      .
